newsitem.title: USA: "Severe damage" needed to stop UPS strike -Clinton.
newsitem.headline: "Severe damage" needed to stop UPS strike -Clinton.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday that the Teamsters union strike against United Parcel Service must result in "severe damage" to the country before he could intervene to halt it.

Speaking at a press conference, Clinton said he could only halt the strike by invoking a rarely-used Taft-Hartley law on industrial relations. "There has to be a severe damage to the country. The test (in that law) is ... very high before the president can intervene."

Clinton said that high standard had not been met. He also said there were significant differences between that law and a separate one that governed a dispute between American Airlines and its pilots earlier this year, in which he intervened.
"It's a totally different law from the law that affected the American Airlines case," he said.
"We've done everything we could, both privately as well as publicly, to urge the parties to get back to the table and settle this," Clinton said, adding that he was very concerned for UPS customers.
Thousands of members of the Teamsters union were on strike for a third day after talks on a new contract broke down late on Sunday. No new talks have been scheduled.
